questions.stem: The 'CHERAW' folk dance, performed by weaving in and out of clapping bamboo poles, belongs to which state?

options.option_text: Nagaland — home of the Hornbill Festival dances
Mizoram — performed by the Mizo community
Manipur — known for Lai Haraoba folk rituals
Meghalaya — associated with the Khasi tribal belt

questions.explanation: Cheraw, popularly called the Bamboo Dance, is the most celebrated folk dance of Mizoram, performed by the Mizo people. Long bamboo poles are clapped together rhythmically while dancers step in and out. Nagaland and Manipur are common distractors from the North-East cluster but are incorrect.

questions.stem: The folk dance 'NATI' of Himachal Pradesh is especially notable in the world of folk arts because it is:

options.option_text: A martial folk dance performed exclusively by hill men
A dance form granted Geographical Indication status in 2010
Largest folk dance, holding an entry in the Guinness World Records
The only North Indian dance on UNESCO's intangible heritage list

questions.explanation: Nati of Himachal Pradesh holds the Guinness World Record for the world's largest folk dance, performed in massive groups during fairs and festivals, especially in Kullu and Shimla. It is not a martial dance, has no GI tag, and is not listed on UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage register.

questions.stem: The 'WANGALA' festival — sometimes called the Hundred Drums Festival — is the harvest celebration dance of which tribal community of Meghalaya?

options.option_text: Khasi tribe — inhabiting the Khasi Hills of central Meghalaya
Garo tribe — celebrating the post-harvest season in western Meghalaya
Jaintia tribe — belonging to the Jaintia Hills of eastern Meghalaya
Bodo tribe — a plains tribal community straddling Assam and Meghalaya

questions.explanation: Wangala is the most important harvest festival of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya, performed to thank the Sun God Saljong. The resonant beating of drums gives it the 'Hundred Drums' title. The Khasi and Jaintia tribes also inhabit Meghalaya but have separate festivals; Bodo is primarily an Assam tribe.

questions.stem: 'BAGURUMBA', celebrated for its graceful swaying movements and nicknamed the butterfly dance, is the folk dance of which tribal community of Assam?

options.option_text: Dimasa tribe of Assam, performed during paddy harvesting season
Bodo tribe of Assam, performed during the Bwisagu spring festival
Rabha tribe of Assam, associated with the worship of goddess Kali
Mising tribe of Assam, linked to the Ali-Aye-Ligang crop festival

questions.explanation: Bagurumba is the folk dance of the Bodo tribe of Assam, performed during Bwisagu (the Bodo new year/spring festival). Its light, flowing movements inspired the 'butterfly dance' nickname. The Mising tribe's Ali-Aye-Ligang and the Dimasa harvest dance are distinct traditions and common distractors.

questions.stem: 'DOLLU KUNITHA' is a vigorous folk dance of Karnataka's Kuruba shepherd community. The term 'DOLLU' specifically refers to:

options.option_text: A large cylindrical drum central to the performance
The colourful silk costume worn exclusively by male dancers
A deity revered by the Kuruba pastoral shepherd community
The bamboo pole around which dancers circle in formation

questions.explanation: In Dollu Kunitha, 'Dollu' means a large cylindrical drum in Kannada, and 'Kunitha' means dance. Performers beat these drums while dancing simultaneously, creating a powerful spectacle. It is performed in honour of Lord Beereshwara. Options B and D describe props from other dance traditions and are designed to mislead.

questions.stem: The ritualistic folk dance 'PONUNG' of Arunachal Pradesh is performed by which tribal community and during which specific festival?

options.option_text: Nyishi tribe — performed during the Boori Boot festival marking the new year
Adi tribe — performed during the Porag festival as a harvest celebration
Apatani tribe — performed at the Myoko festival for inter-village social bonding
Wancho tribe — performed during funerary rites held in the Longding district

questions.explanation: Ponung is the folk dance of the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, performed during the Porag festival — a harvest and fertility celebration. It is a group dance led by a Miri (shaman/priest) who chants while women dance in a circle. The Apatani Myoko and Nyishi Boori Boot are separate tribal festivals and are the most plausible distractors.

questions.stem: 'PULI KALI' (Tiger Play), where performers paint their bodies as tigers and leopards, is performed on which specific day of the Onam festival and is most prominently associated with which district?

options.option_text: Fourth day (Naluambu Onam) — celebrated most prominently in Thrissur district
Tenth day (Thiruvonam) — the main feast day, centred in Thiruvananthapuram district
First day (Atham) — marking the formal start of Onam, rooted in Palakkad district
Eighth day (Pooradam) — linked to Vallamkali boat race preparations in Alappuzha

questions.explanation: Puli Kali is performed on the fourth day of Onam (Naluambu Onam), most famously in Thrissur district, where thousands of body-painted performers recreate hunting scenes. Thiruvonam (10th day) is the most celebrated day of Onam and a classic distractor, but Puli Kali precedes it and is centred in Thrissur, not Thiruvananthapuram.
